name: timedog
description: Lists files that were saved by a backup of the macOS Time Machine

repo.name: timedog
repo.description: Displays set of files that were saved in Time Machine backups

readme.summary: Good usage documentation with solid examples and troubleshooting, but lacks any installation instructions beyond 'unzip to Desktop'.
readme.top_issue: No installation instructions — no mention of dependencies (Perl version, modules), how to obtain the script, or how to make it executable.

injection_risks.description: The 'subprocess' module is used without input validation, which could lead to command injection attacks if user-controlled data is passed to it.
The 'os.system' function is not explicitly used, but the 'subprocess' module is used with 'shell=True', which could lead to shell injection attacks if user-controlled data is passed to it.

critical_findings: Potential command injection attacks through the 'subprocess' module
Lack of input validation for user-controlled data
security.summary: The timecopy.py script has some security concerns, including potential command injection attacks and lack of input validation, but does not appear to expose sensitive information or use insecure defaults.

common_complaints: Compatibility issues with newer macOS versions (Big Sur, Mojave, APFS)
Tool fails to detect Time Machine backups or reports zero backups
Terminal permission issues accessing Time Machine volumes
Doesn't work with encrypted Time Machine backups
No support for multiple Time Machine disks
praise_themes: Longevity and reliability when it works
Useful community resource for Time Machine analysis
sentiment.summary: The project shows poor community health with critical macOS compatibility bugs unresolved for 4+ years, recent 2024 issues still open, patch submissions ignored, and long-dormant feature requests with zero engagement indicating active abandonment.

communication.summary: The maintainer responses are generally helpful and patient, though the technical depth could be improved.

concerns: No commits in 17 months (last commit October 2024)
7 open issues with zero resolution in 6+ months
maintenance.summary: timedog is abandoned with over a year of inactivity and multiple unaddressed issues indicating no active maintenance.

analysis_summary.doc_summary: The README provides a clear and concise introduction to the package, but lacks installation instructions and has some areas for improvement in configuration and troubleshooting documentation.
concerns: No commits in the past six months
Docs: Installation instructions are not provided
Security: Potential command injection attacks through the 'subprocess' module
Security: Lack of input validation for user-controlled data
highlights: Six contributors active in the past six months
